notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: the latest EGX close is Thursday 19 November (EGX30 51,458.04); the EGX reopens on Sunday. Wall Street, gold and oil are Friday 20 November closes. Gold prices in EGP are Banky's Friday prices. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Brent's exact Friday settlement, because Reuters puts it at $92.57 and Investing.com at $92.49 (the brief shows about $92.5 and flags the chart); Brent's weekly fall, given as 3.5% by Investing.com and near 4% by Reuters; Thursday's net flows by nationality, because Amwal Al Ghad reports non-Arab foreigners as net buyers of EGP 1.97 bn while EnterpriseAM reports international investors as the only net sellers; Thursday's breadth; a CBE dollar rate newer than 18 November; the IRGC's claim to have downed a US drone. Egypt Aluminum's 17 November row on StockAnalysis remains inconsistent (a -0.30% change against a 5.2% fall in the closes).
notes.sourcesFoot: All 21 StockAnalysis pages opened on Saturday and show Thursday 19 November as the latest session.

items: An AI-led sell-off hits markets: the Nasdaq falls 2.3% on Thursday and Asian indices drop up to 6.8% on Friday → Anthropic's record IPO does not calm AI-bubble fears.
Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027 → higher pay supports spending but raises costs for labour-heavy firms.
The EGX30 slips 0.17% to 51,458.04 as Telecom Egypt falls 3.47% → turnover is 43.9% below the 90-day average.
Gold drops to a 14-month low of $3,554 and heads for a 9% weekly loss → markets price a 97.3% chance of a Fed hike in December.

The IMF reaches a staff-level agreement on Egypt's final EFF review and third RSF review, worth about $2.3 bn → board approval before 15 December would close the programme and support the pound and Egypt's credit standing.
Egypt's economy grows 4.9% in July to September, up from 4.7%, while unemployment rises to 6.0% → growth holds up despite the war, rate hike and gas cuts.
Orascom Construction's nine-month profit nearly doubles to $218 mn as its backlog reaches $11.6 bn → strong awards support the stock ahead of the OCI merger listing on 24 November.
Gold falls 3.2% on Wednesday to its lowest close since September 2025; 21K in Egypt drops to EGP 5,750 → Fed minutes show almost all officials see more hikes ahead.

Misr Insurance Holding will sell 15% of Misr Life Insurance on the EGX in December, with EFG Hermes as sole bookrunner → the IMF wants about $1.5 bn of asset sales before the programme ends; Banque du Caire has delivered $658 mn so far.
EGX30 falls 0.99% to 51,682 on Tuesday and the EGX70 drops another 2.42% → local investors are the sole net sellers as small caps extend their slide.
Gold drops below $3,800 as Fed officials signal more rate hikes; 21K gold in Egypt slips to EGP 5,900 → higher US yields and a firm dollar weigh on bullion and on emerging-market carry.
The Arab Energy Fund files a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive at $0.70 a share → Gulf money keeps buying into EGX-listed energy services.

Seven fertiliser makers agree to pay 50% more for gas, $12.75 per mmBtu and $175 mn upfront, in return for exporting their full output until early January → the state recovers some LNG costs while producers keep selling urea at about $535 a tonne; gas cuts of 20-40% stay.
EGX30 ends flat at 52,200 on Monday but the EGX70 drops 3.76% and the EGX100 2.88% → small caps sell off while Edita (+7.4%) and Telecom Egypt (+5.2%) hold up the blue-chip index.
Edita posts record quarterly revenue of EGP 7.3 bn, up 32.9%, with profit up 41.5% → volume growth and pricing lift the snack maker, and the stock jumps 7.44%.
Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd move three more Gemini services back to the Suez Canal from December → more Asia-Europe traffic adds to canal revenue and dollar inflows.

Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027, covering about 26.5 mn workers → higher wages lift consumer spending but raise costs for labour-heavy industries.
TMG Holding's nine-month profit rises 11.9% to EGP 11.72 bn, Fawry's 32% and Edita's 54% → earnings season keeps delivering growth for EGX blue chips.
ONE's container ship crosses the Suez Canal and three more Premier Alliance services are set to follow → the return of Asian carriers adds to canal revenue and dollar inflows.
EGX30 rises 0.31% to 52,187 on Sunday, led by Orascom Construction (+3.4%) and AMOC (+4.8%) → the index is up 24.8% this year, though turnover runs 17% below its 90-day average.

stories.h: Wall Street falls into correction after its worst week since April 2025
stories.what: The Nasdaq Composite falls 5.3% to 22,617.73 on Friday, the S&P 500 3.5% to 6,924.67 and the Dow 1.9% to 48,147.42. Anthropic trades at $87.95 at midday, 9.5% below Thursday's close, against an IPO price of $83.30. In Asia on Friday, Taiwan's Taiex falls 6.2%, Seoul's Kospi 5.2% and Tokyo's Nikkei 5.1%.
stories.why: Fears over debt-funded AI spending and Nvidia's leadership change drive the sell-off.
stories.aff: Global equities, tech stocks and risk appetite.
stories.eg: Risk-off moods tend to slow foreign flows into Egyptian assets.
stories.egx: Bearish for sentiment at Sunday's open.

key.l: spot gold's weekly fall to 20 Nov

stories.h: Gold posts its worst week in eight months; 21K in Egypt drops 3%
stories.what: Spot gold falls 2.4% to settle at $3,538.11 on Friday and drops 8.9% on the week. Fed Governor Christopher Waller backs a 50 bp hike in December, and Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson says another increase is needed. In Egypt, Banky's 21K price falls EGP 175, or 3.04%, to EGP 5,575 a gram.
stories.why: Rate-hike bets and margin calls from the AI rout push investors to sell gold.

key.l: war-risk insurance per barrel, Middle East to East Asia

stories.h: Coalition intercepts Houthi missiles over Riyadh as Gulf shipping costs climb
stories.what: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepts three ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh overnight, days after a Houthi strike hit the Public Investment Fund tower. It says it hit Houthi sites including Sanaa on Friday. A US Maritime Administration memo, reported by Al Jazeera, warns that Hormuz risk is spreading; the IMO counts about 130 attacks on vessels and at least 25 seafarers killed since the war began.
stories.why: The US-Israeli war on Iran spreads to Saudi Arabia and shipping lanes.
stories.aff: Gulf security, tanker insurance, Red Sea and Hormuz shipping.
stories.eg: Higher war-risk costs weigh on Suez Canal traffic and Egypt's import bill.
stories.egx: Bearish for shipping and import-heavy sectors.

stories.h: Oil edges up on Friday but posts a third weekly loss
stories.what: Brent settles at about $92.5 on Friday, up about 0.6%; Reuters gives $92.57 and Investing.com $92.49. Iran war worries and short-covering lift prices, while Hormuz shipments are back near pre-war levels and the IEA forecasts a surplus.
stories.why: Supply recovers while Gulf attacks continue.
stories.eg: Brent near $92 keeps Egypt's energy costs steady.

stories.h: Arab Energy Fund bids $70 mn for 21.3% of Maridive
stories.what: The Arab Energy Fund launches a tender offer for 100 mn shares, or 21.3%, of Maridive & Oil Services at $0.70 a share, worth $70 mn. EFG Hermes is the sole adviser. Separately, Misr Insurance Holding plans to float 15% of Misr Life Insurance on the EGX next month.
stories.why: EnterpriseAM gives no reason for the bid.
stories.aff: Maridive's shareholders and the EGX's M&A pipeline.
stories.eg: Gulf capital keeps buying into Egyptian energy services.
stories.egx: Bullish for Maridive and the brokers advising on deals.

key.l: Deutsche Bank's EGP per USD scenarios

stories.h: Deutsche Bank ties the pound's path to the Iran war
stories.what: Deutsche Bank Research sees the pound strengthening to 48 per dollar if the US and Iran reach a lasting deal, and weakening beyond 60 if the war escalates. Banks quote an average of 53.78 buy and 53.88 sell on 18 November, Amwal Al Ghad reports.
stories.why: The war drives oil prices, shipping costs and portfolio flows into Egypt.
stories.aff: The pound, inflation and foreign holdings of Egyptian debt.
stories.eg: A deal would ease pressure on the pound; escalation would add to it.
stories.egx: Neutral; exporters gain from a weaker pound, importers lose.

key.l: end of the FRA's consumer-finance licence freeze

stories.h: FRA extends its freeze on new consumer-finance and microfinance licences
stories.what: The Financial Regulatory Authority extends its freeze on new consumer-finance and microfinance licences through the traditional route to 11 October 2027. The freeze on fintech consumer-finance licences runs to 25 February 2027.
stories.why: EnterpriseAM gives no reason for the extension.
stories.eg: Existing licence holders face less new competition.

stories.h: EGX30 ends the week with a third straight loss
stories.what: The EGX30 falls 0.17% to 51,458.04 on Thursday after losses on Tuesday and Wednesday; market cap is EGP 4.06 tn. Turnover is EGP 6.2 bn, 43.9% below the 90-day average. Edita (+2.94%) gains, while Telecom Egypt (-3.47%) and Orascom Construction (-1.93%) fall.
stories.why: The sources give no single cause; the index is up 23.0% this year.
stories.eg: Thin turnover shows caution before a volatile global weekend.
